title: Build a take-apart 3D model to learn how a drone flies
summary: A poster had Claude Code build an interactive drone model from one prompt; they say it worked out the propeller spin directions, checked every frame and wrote motor sounds.
agent_role: Claude Code built the drone part by part from a single prompt, worked out the propeller directions, checked the visuals in a hidden browser and wrote the sound. The human asked the question and gave the prompt.
outcome: Author reports a working take-apart drone model with spinning props, motor sound and a playground.
what_they_did: The poster wanted to understand how a drone stays in the air. They asked Claude Code to build a drone they could take apart, using a free add-on for anatomy-style models. Claude built it part by part and checked each frame in a hidden browser window.
how_it_went: They say Claude worked out on its own that two propellers spin clockwise and two counter-clockwise so the twist cancels. It also wrote a soundtrack in code, with the motor whirr rising as the propellers speed up.
worth_knowing: Having the agent check its own output in a browser helped catch visual details, like propellers blurring into discs at high speed.
prompt: Build me an interactive 3D model of a [object, e.g. drone] that I can take apart piece by piece to learn how it works. Add each part one at a time and label it. Explain the key physics in plain words, and make the model show it in motion. Open the result in a browser and check each step looks right before moving on. Show me your plan for the parts first and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: Claude Code built and self-checked an interactive drone model to learn how drones fly, an original educational use. Evidence is the author's thread only, and the full build sits in a linked article.
